PROJECTS	

RRCP

 06/2023 - Present

Project# 1. June 2023 to present

Title: RRCP – Regulatory Reporting & Control Platform.

Environment: JDK 1.8, Spring Boot, Oracle, JavaScript, REST API, Microservices, Jenkins, Ansible, JMS, Git, Docker, K8S, AWS (S3, EC2, Elastic Beanstalk, EKS, RDS, CloudWatch & AWS Lambda).

Team Size: 10 Role: Developer Description:

I contributed to the development of the RRCP application, utilizing cutting-edge technologies such as Spring Boot, microservices, REST API, and Oracle for database management. The architecture includes a Data Service Layer (DSL) platform, with services such as Acquisition Manager, Delivery Service, Adapter Service, and Feedback Service deployed on the Internal Kubernetes Platform (IKP).

Communication between services is facilitated through Solace MQ.

The system handles various types of PTS sources, including XFOS, MARTINI, HTDE, and more. Trade files are received from the DSL

source via MQ, processed, and subjected to business logic to generate output XML, which is then transmitted to the DTCC system. All files undergo validation at DTCC, and upon compliance with the schema, a response is sent back to our Feedback Service. This service, in turn, publishes the response to the notification service, indicating whether the response is an acknowledgment (ACK) or a negative acknowledgment (NACK).

I played a key role in this project, contributing to the successful implementation of the system.

Project# 2: June 2021 to June 2023

Title: SFTR - Securities Finance & Trade Reporting.

Environment: JDK 1.8, Spring Boot, Oracle, JavaScript, Rest API, Microservices, Jenkins, Ansible, JMS, Git, Docker & Kubernetes, AWS(S3, EC2, Elastic Beanstalk, EKS, RDS, Cloudwatch & AWS Lambda).

Team size: 6 Role: Developer Description:

During the project duration from June 2021 to June 2023, our team utilized cutting-edge technologies such as Spring Boot,

microservices, RESTful APIs, and Oracle database to develop the SFTR application. The platform consisted of a robust Data Service

Layer (DSL), with all services including Acquisition Manager, Delivery Service, Adapter Service, and Feedback Service deployed on the Internal Kubernetes Platform (IKP). This enabled us to ensure seamless and efficient operations.

Project# 3

Title: PFM(Personal Finance Manager)

Environment: JDK 1.8, Spring boot, Oracle, JavaScript, Rest api and Tomcat Server. Team size: 5

Role: Developer Description:

We developed the PFM application using Spring boot, Java 8, and REST API. This application allows users to invest in a mutual fund and offers modules for investing, redeeming, SIP, and SWP. Users can log in to the application through their mobile or desktop to view their investments on the dashboard. They can also invest and redeem the amount as per their needs.

Responsibilities:

Interacting with Customer to understand requirements

Developed Microservices for all modules.

Conduct code review, ensure adherence to coding standards and implement best practices to maintain code quality.

Identify, troubleshoot and resolve technical issues and bugs within applications.

Stay updated with new java technologies, frameworks, and industry trends to incorporate innovative solutions.

Develop and maintain technical documentation for applications and systems.

Ensure smooth coordination within the development teamand with other teams involved in the project.

Resolving the production issues reported by the client users

Write database queries for fetching data from Database

Created a utilities to build code in a fast and efficient.

Enhance the code to overcome duplicate task

Enhance the development by using th utility to generate FTL template along with feature files.

What was a successful outcome of your work? (e.g. Raised $3,000 for the charity)

sections.label: Projects
sections.text:
PROJECTS	
RRCP
 06/2023 - Present
Project# 1. June 2023 to present
Title: RRCP – Regulatory Reporting & Control Platform.
Environment: JDK 1.8, Spring Boot, Oracle, JavaScript, REST API, Microservices, Jenkins, Ansible, JMS, Git, Docker, K8S, AWS (S3, EC2, Elastic Beanstalk, EKS, RDS, CloudWatch & AWS Lambda).
Team Size: 10 Role: Developer Description:
I contributed to the development of the RRCP application, utilizing cutting-edge technologies such as Spring Boot, microservices, REST API, and Oracle for database management. The architecture includes a Data Service Layer (DSL) platform, with services such as Acquisition Manager, Delivery Service, Adapter Service, and Feedback Service deployed on the Internal Kubernetes Platform (IKP).
Communication between services is facilitated through Solace MQ.
The system handles various types of PTS sources, including XFOS, MARTINI, HTDE, and more. Trade files are received from the DSL
source via MQ, processed, and subjected to business logic to generate output XML, which is then transmitted to the DTCC system. All files undergo validation at DTCC, and upon compliance with the schema, a response is sent back to our Feedback Service. This service, in turn, publishes the response to the notification service, indicating whether the response is an acknowledgment (ACK) or a negative acknowledgment (NACK).
I played a key role in this project, contributing to the successful implementation of the system.
Project# 2: June 2021 to June 2023
Title: SFTR - Securities Finance & Trade Reporting.
Environment: JDK 1.8, Spring Boot, Oracle, JavaScript, Rest API, Microservices, Jenkins, Ansible, JMS, Git, Docker & Kubernetes, AWS(S3, EC2, Elastic Beanstalk, EKS, RDS, Cloudwatch & AWS Lambda).
Team size: 6 Role: Developer Description:
During the project duration from June 2021 to June 2023, our team utilized cutting-edge technologies such as Spring Boot,
microservices, RESTful APIs, and Oracle database to develop the SFTR application. The platform consisted of a robust Data Service
Layer (DSL), with all services including Acquisition Manager, Delivery Service, Adapter Service, and Feedback Service deployed on the Internal Kubernetes Platform (IKP). This enabled us to ensure seamless and efficient operations.
Project# 3
Title: PFM(Personal Finance Manager)
Environment: JDK 1.8, Spring boot, Oracle, JavaScript, Rest api and Tomcat Server. Team size: 5
Role: Developer Description:
We developed the PFM application using Spring boot, Java 8, and REST API. This application allows users to invest in a mutual fund and offers modules for investing, redeeming, SIP, and SWP. Users can log in to the application through their mobile or desktop to view their investments on the dashboard. They can also invest and redeem the amount as per their needs.
Responsibilities:
Interacting with Customer to understand requirements
Developed Microservices for all modules.
Conduct code review, ensure adherence to coding standards and implement best practices to maintain code quality.
Identify, troubleshoot and resolve technical issues and bugs within applications.
Stay updated with new java technologies, frameworks, and industry trends to incorporate innovative solutions.
Develop and maintain technical documentation for applications and systems.
Ensure smooth coordination within the development teamand with other teams involved in the project.
Resolving the production issues reported by the client users
Write database queries for fetching data from Database
Created a utilities to build code in a fast and efficient.
Enhance the code to overcome duplicate task
Enhance the development by using th utility to generate FTL template along with feature files.
What was a successful outcome of your work? (e.g. Raised $3,000 for the charity)
